whatFailed: POST /v2/bookings with a `routing` object and `cal-api-version: 2026-02-25` returned 400 complaining that top-level `timeZone`, `language` and `metadata` are missing, because Cal.diy does not know the 2026-02-25 version and silently validated the body against the 2024-04-15 input shape.

docClaim.quote: routing: Routing information from routing forms that determined the booking assignment. Both responseId and teamMemberIds are required if provided. ... Routing: queuedResponseId: The ID of the queued form response. Only present if the form response was queued. responseId: The ID of the routing form response. teamMemberIds: Array of team member IDs that were routed to handle this booking. teamMemberEmail: The email of the team member assigned to handle this booking. ... parameters: - name: cal-api-version, in: header, description: Must be set to 2026-02-25, required: true
docClaim.section: create-a-booking/openapi (request body `routing`, lines 242-253 and 397-408 and 559-570; `Routing` schema lines 843-899; `cal-api-version` header lines 85-92)

observed: HTTP 400 in 64 ms with body {"status":"error",...,"error":{"code":"BadRequestException","message":"Bad Request Exception","details":{"errors":[{"property":"timeZone","constraints":{"isTimeZone":"timeZone must be a valid IANA time-zone"}},{"property":"language",...},{"property":"metadata",...}]}}}. The echoed `target` is only {start, eventTypeId}: the whitelisting validator had already stripped `attendee` and `routing` off the payload, so the routing object never reached any handler. No booking was created and steps 2 and 3 never ran.
impact: A developer following cal.com's published Create-a-booking page cannot book through a routing form on Cal.diy at all: the documented API version is rejected outright, and even on the newest version Cal.diy does ship (2024-08-13) routing forms no longer exist in the product, so there is nothing to route from and nothing to echo back. Doc-following harm, no data loss.

rootCause.explanation: Two layers. (1) The immediate 400: the NestJS custom version extractor at bootstrap.ts:31-41 returns the header value only when it is a member of API_VERSIONS, otherwise it falls through to VERSION_2024_04_15. packages/platform/constants/api.ts:56-68 in the tested tree lists only 2024-06-14, 2024-06-11, 2024-04-15, 2024-08-13 and 2024-09-04, so `2026-02-25` is unknown and is silently downgraded rather than refused. The request is then routed to the 2024-04-15 controller and validated against CreateBookingInput_2024_04_15 (apps/api/v2/src/platform/bookings/2024-04-15/inputs/create-booking.input.ts:91-146), whose shape is flat and whose `timeZone` (@IsTimeZone, line 122-124), `language` (@IsString, line 137) and `metadata` (@IsObject, lines 144-146) are all required, producing exactly the three constraint errors seen; the nested `attendee` and `routing` objects are not in that class and are whitelist-stripped. (2) The deeper reason the scenario can never pass on Cal.diy: routing forms are Cal.com team/enterprise code and were removed from the fork. The tested tree has no packages/app-store/routing-forms directory, no packages/features/ee directory, no App_RoutingForms_Form / App_RoutingForms_FormResponse / App_RoutingForms_QueuedFormResponse / RoutingFormResponseDenormalized / RoutingTrace models in packages/prisma/schema.prisma, and migration packages/prisma/migrations/20260305043434_remove_routing_forms/migration.sql drops all of those tables plus the ROUTING_FORM_ROUTING assignment reasons and the ROUTING_FORM_FALLBACK_HIT webhook trigger. The identifier `routingFormResponseId` appears nowhere in packages/ or apps/. A vestigial `routing` property does survive on CreateBookingInput_2024_08_13 (packages/platform/types/bookings/2024-08-13/inputs/create-booking.input.ts:154-247 for the `Routing` class, 376-388 for the property), but apps/api/v2/src/platform/bookings/2024-08-13/services/input.service.ts:200-221 (getRoutingFormData) maps only teamMemberIds, teamMemberEmail, skipContactOwner, crmAppSlug and crmOwnerRecordType, and deliberately drops `responseId`. There is no `routing` object in any 2024-08-13 output DTO or in output.service.ts, so `data.routing.responseId` and `data.routing.queuedResponseId` cannot exist in a Cal.diy response on any shipped version.

introducedBy.title: refactor: Cal.diy
introducedBy.note: The single EE-strip commit. It deleted packages/app-store/routing-forms/ and packages/features/ee/, added migration 20260305043434_remove_routing_forms, removed the App_RoutingForms_* Prisma models, and removed `routingFormResponseId` from the 2024-08-13 bookings input service (git log -S confirms; the field was added by #22239, 2025-07-04, and lived until #28903). The separate, older half of the failure is the API version list in packages/platform/constants/api.ts, last touched by dcf10935de (#25739, 2026-01-07) and never advanced past 2024-09-04, plus the silent-downgrade extractor in bootstrap.ts; that code is not new, the mismatch is that cal.com's docs moved to 2026-02-25 and the fork's version list did not.

notes: Answers to the two questions the brief asks for a systemic-cause-1 failure. (a) Would the scenario also fail on a version Cal.diy does have? Yes. On cal-api-version 2024-08-13 the body would validate (CreateBookingInput_2024_08_13 has nested `attendee` and an optional `routing` object whose `responseId` and `teamMemberIds` are both required once the object is present, matching the doc sentence, so steps 2 and 3 would probably pass), but step 1 would still fail: there is no `routing` key in any 2024-08-13 booking output DTO and output.service.ts never emits one, so `data.routing.responseId` and `data.routing.queuedResponseId` are unresolvable. The `hosts[0].id` / `hosts[0].email` half could pass, since BookingHost (packages/platform/types/bookings/2024-08-13/outputs/booking.output.ts:87-106) does carry id and email and qualified-hosts.service.ts:31-66 does narrow hosts to routedTeamMemberIds. (b) Is there a Cal.diy-side defect independent of the version? Two worth reporting. First, `Routing.responseId` is declared required (@IsInt, non-optional) on the 2024-08-13 input, so callers are forced to supply a routing-form response id, yet getRoutingFormData silently discards it and there is no App_RoutingForms_FormResponse table for it to refer to: a required field that is impossible to satisfy meaningfully and is dropped without a word. Second, the whole `routing` object is dead weight in the fork; the maintainers' own cleanup PRs (#29025, #29030) call routing-form events 'unsupported' but both were closed unmerged, so the vestige remains. Also worth flagging to the doc author: the bound page is internally inconsistent. Its operationId is BookingsController_2026_02_25_createBooking and it mandates cal-api-version 2026-02-25, but its request and response schemas are still named CreateBookingInput_2024_08_13 / CreateBookingOutput_2024_08_13, and the Routing schema appears only under the request body, never in BookingOutput_2024_08_13 (lines 901-1000), so the scenario's expectation of a `data.routing` echo is an extrapolation the page does not actually make. Separately, no real routing-form response could have been seeded: with the App_RoutingForms_* tables dropped, whatever value `{{fixture:teamEventTypeRouting.responseId}}` resolved to was necessarily a synthetic integer. Team and Membership models are still present in the fork's schema, so the team event type itself was fine; the README's 'Teams removed' refers to the paid team features, not the data model.
